description: Frontmatter, section structure, section word caps and token budget for a feat spec in docs/feat/. The prose authorities are docs/__meta__/feat.md section 2 for the frontmatter, section 4 for the structure and section 6 for the caps and the budget; this file is their machine-checkable half. It is the base layer: a namespace layer, feat-<namespace>.structure.json, is applied on its own beside it and can only add to it. It states what every feat spec carries whatever its type or namespace: Summary, Table of Contents and Key Concepts open it, the optional sections keep their relative order, sections the document invents for itself follow them, and References then Code References close it, both being references: one to other documents, one to the code. Usage and Code References are optional here for every type; which type requires or forbids them is a prose rule in feat.md section 4, checked by review, never a condition here. The word caps keep each section's prose concise: a word is a whitespace-delimited token of prose, and fenced code blocks and table rows are not counted, since examples and reference tables are what a feat spec is for. A section's cap covers its H3 children, and the cap on the `any` run applies to each of its sections alone. Table of Contents, References and Code References carry no cap: each is a list of links. Each named section also carries a `description`, what the section holds, and `examples`, samples of its body drawn from the corpus's own documents: an author whose document lacks the section is shown the description and the first example, and the rest serve a reader of this file. The token budget is on the whole file, frontmatter, code and tables included: what loading it costs an agent, in o200k_base tokens whichever agent reads it.

name.description: Kebab-case. Must match the filename minus .md, which the checker verifies separately.

allOf.$comment: The trigger clause naming the questions this document answers.

type.description: meta groups a feature area, feature documents a user-facing capability, component documents an internal building block.

status.description: Feature maturity. States where the feature stands today; never a version number.

components.description: Comma-separated, each entry prefixed module: (a top-level package of lorecraft, as in lorecraft.project, and nothing deeper), skill: (a skill directory, kebab-case), or spec: (a meta spec name under docs/__meta__/, kebab-case). The pattern fixes the prefix vocabulary, the character set, and that a module: entry is lorecraft.<package>; that a skill: or spec: entry is kebab-case is stated in feat.md section 2 and verified by reading, because one regular expression covering every prefix's spelling is less readable than the rule it encodes.

outline.description: Two to four sentences expanding on the frontmatter description: what the feature does, why it exists and its primary use.
examples:
`lorecraft check` checks the whole workspace in one run: every document under `docs/` against the meta specs
in `docs/__meta__/`, and every agent skill against the Agent Skills specification. Each rule has a code, such as
`FM001`, in a group named by its prefix. It prints a diagnostic per rule broken, and exits `1` when any is an error.

outline.description: Links to the sections below it, one numbered entry per section, starting at Key Concepts.
The terms the document uses, defined once, in one line each; a term the whole toolkit uses is linked to the glossary instead of defined again.
examples:
- **Root**: The directory that holds `docs/__meta__/`; every path lorecraft prints is relative to it.
- **Corpus**: A directory directly under `docs/` whose documents meta specs govern, named by the
  directory.
- **Document**: A Markdown file directly inside a corpus directory.
- **Workspace model**: The corpora, their meta specs and their documents, as found in one snapshot.

outline.description: How the feature fits together: data flow and component interaction. Included only when the flow is not obvious from the usage examples.
examples:
### Root Discovery

Without `--root`, the root is the nearest of the working directory and its parents that holds a
`docs/__meta__/` directory. With `--root`, the given directory is the root, and it must exist. Either way it is
resolved with symlinks followed, and every path printed is relative to it.

### One Run, One Snapshot

Every rule reads the same snapshot, through one database, so a file is read and parsed once however many rules
read it. Every meta spec is loaded and validated before any subject is checked, so one malformed
meta spec stops the whole run.

outline.description: Options, their defaults and where they are read from, usually as a table.
examples:
| Key | Value | Meaning |
|-----|-------|---------|
| `empty_sections` | `"forbidden"` | Every heading must have content under it |
| `outline` | list of entries | `{"section": "<name>"}`, with `"optional": true` when it may be left out, or `{"any": true}` |
| `forbidden` | list of names | Sections that must not appear anywhere |

Every key is optional.

outline.description: How to invoke the feature, with working examples in fenced blocks: the command a reader types and what it prints. Required for a feature document, forbidden for a meta document.
examples:
```bash
# Every rule over the workspace around the working directory
lorecraft check

# Another repository, as JSON
lorecraft check --root ../other-repo --format json
```

A document with no frontmatter, under a corpus whose structure file states a frontmatter schema:

```text
docs/code/guide.md:1: error[FM001]: no `---` delimited frontmatter block
  = note: the frontmatter schema is set here (docs/__meta__/code.structure.json)
checked 1 subject(s): 1 error(s), 0 warning(s)
```

### Caps and a Budget

```json
{
  "$schema": "../schemas/structure.spec.json",
  "tokens": 5000,
  "outline": [
    { "any": true, "words": 350 },
    { "section": "Checklist", "words": 250 },
    { "section": "References", "optional": true }
  ]
}
```

Each section a document names for itself holds at most 350 words, `Checklist` at most 250, and `References`
is not capped. The whole file holds at most 5000 tokens.

outline.description: The feature's known constraints, as a short list.
examples:
- The command takes no paths, and no option sets a level: every rule runs at its default level, and a selection
  only narrows which run.
- A repository with skills and no `docs/__meta__/` needs `--root`.
- A check covers what a machine can decide. Whether a section says what it should stays with review.

outline.description: Cross-references to other feat specs, one per line with the relationship named first (Dependency, Alternative, Related, Extended by or Base), linking up to the base and never down to an extension.
examples:
- [cli](cli.md) - Base: the command line and the options every command shares
- [workspace](workspace.md) - Dependency: the documents, skills and snapshot the command reads
- [spec](spec.md) - Dependency: the meta spec files the rules read

outline.description: The source files behind the feature, one entry per line and never wrapped, each naming a file and how it relates to the feature without explaining its logic. Required for a component document, forbidden for a meta document.
examples:
- `src/lorecraft/cli/commands/check.py` - Declares the command and its options
- `src/lorecraft/cli/check_run.py` - Runs rules and sets the exit status
- `src/lorecraft/cli/root.py` - Root discovery
- `src/lorecraft/checks/runner.py` - Runs every enabled rule over each subject
